story_type: retired warship sunk by live strikes in a sinking exercise
hook: This retired warship took hit after hit until it sank.
narration: This retired Navy ship took hit after hit, more than two hundred nautical miles off Guam.
It was the decommissioned USS Juneau, turned into a target.
In June twenty twenty six, U.S. forces and their allies lined up air, surface and undersea strikes against it.
Ground crews loaded live weapons onto patrol planes.
No simulator can match this: a real weapon, aimed at a real ship.
Infrared cameras watched the hull burn and smoke.
Another blast threw water higher than the ship.
outcome: And the former USS Juneau sank into the Philippine Sea.
title: Warship sunk on purpose off Guam
description:
During Valiant Shield 2026, U.S. joint forces and allies conducted a live-fire sinking exercise in the Philippine Sea on June 27, 2026, more than 200 nautical miles off Guam. The former USS Juneau sank after the coordinated strikes.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by Chief Mass Communication Specialist Ramon Go, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1013423

question_comment: Should old warships be sunk as targets or turned into museums?

extra_sources.excerpt: The exercise occurred more than 200 nautical miles off the coast of Guam, and brought together air, surface, and subsurface assets in coordinated strikes, allowing crews to sharpen critical skills in weapons employment and target engagement under realistic conditions that no simulator can fully replicate.

U.S. Pacific Command joint forces, along with allied and partner forces, successfully carried out a live-fire sinking exercise (SINKEX) as part of Valiant Shield 2026 (VS26), more than 200 nautical miles off the coast in the Mariana Islands Range Complex.
The pinnacle event was the sinking exercise (SINKEX) of the decommissioned Austin-class amphibious transport dock USS Juneau (LPD 10) in the Philippine Sea, June 27.
